concept.name: Inflation swap
concept.definition: A derivative in which one party pays a fixed rate and the other pays the realized change in an inflation index (e.g. U.S. CPI-U) on a notional amount, transferring inflation risk. In the standard zero-coupon form, both legs are compounded and exchanged as a single payment at maturity.
concept.intuition: It is a bet or hedge on inflation itself: one side pays a pre-agreed inflation rate, the other pays whatever inflation actually turns out to be.
concept.mechanics: The fixed leg compounds at the agreed fixed rate; the floating leg accrues the realized growth of the reference inflation index (USD uses CPI-U), typically with a publication lag of a few months. In a zero-coupon inflation swap the two compounded amounts are netted and paid once at maturity; the quoted fixed rate is the market's swap-implied inflation level.
concept.formula: Fixed leg payment = N × [(1 + k)^n − 1]; inflation leg payment = N × [I(T)/I(0) − 1], where N is notional, k the fixed swap rate, n the tenor in years, and I the inflation index level.
concept.failure_modes: Index publication lags, revisions, and seasonal patterns complicate pricing and hedging; the market is also less liquid than nominal swaps, and quoted rates embed inflation risk premia just like TIPS breakevens.
concept.misconceptions: The fixed rate on an inflation swap is not a pure inflation forecast; like breakevens, it includes risk and liquidity premia, so it overstates or understates true expected inflation.
concept.example: A pension fund enters a 10-year zero-coupon inflation swap paying a fixed 2.6% and receiving realized CPI-U growth on $50 million notional, hedging its inflation-linked liabilities.

citations.source: ICE (Intercontinental Exchange) SDX Interest Rates Help — Zero Coupon Inflation Swap
